title: SSA is adding AI-assisted contact and disability-evidence processing while outcome and oversight evidence remain open
source_unit: U.S. Social Security Administration FY 2025-2026 Annual Performance Plan, SSA Open Data disability-denial review documentation, and SSA Office of Inspector General ongoing-audit register
geography: United States Social Security Administration; national disability programs and customer-service channels

observations.period: FY 2025-2026 plan; implementation and performance targets

ai_customer_contact.value: AI is being used to enhance Interactive Voice Response tools and promote an SSA chatbot

automated_calls.unit: million automated calls projected in each of FY 2025 and FY 2026

ai_evidence_processing.value: IMAGEN transforms evidence in electronic disability folders into machine-readable text with search and intelligent-analysis capabilities

initial_disability_processing_time.unit: days; FY 2026 planned average processing time for initial disability claims

initial_disability_decisional_accuracy.unit: percent; FY 2026 planned State Disability Determination Services decisional accuracy rate

claimant_outcome.unit: no claimant-level AI exposure, decision, explanation, appeal, correction, payment, or later health/work outcome in the plan

observations.method: Review of SSA's official FY 2025-2026 Annual Performance Plan; agency initiatives, projected automated-call volume, processing targets, and decisional-accuracy targets are retained separately from realized system performance and claimant outcomes.
observations.uncertainty: The plan does not identify which calls or claims receive AI assistance, whether AI changes wait time or accuracy relative to a counterfactual, how errors are detected and corrected, whether users receive explanations, or whether service changes alter benefit receipt, household income, health, work, or trust.
observations.subgroup: SSA customers, disability claimants, beneficiaries, medical providers submitting evidence, teleservice users, State DDS staff, federal examiners, and people with limited digital access or communication accommodations.
observations.counterinterpretation: Automation may reduce routine work and waiting for some users while creating new authentication, escalation, accessibility, or error-correction burdens for others; a target is not evidence of realized improvement.

denominator.unit: DDS jurisdictions included in SSA's targeted review of denied disability cases; all 50 States, DC, and Puerto Rico

ssa_ai_audit.value: SSA OIG lists an audit of SSA's Use of Artificial Intelligence, started 2026-03-30, with planned completion in FY 2027 Q2

denial_review_sampling.value: statistical model identifies denied cases matching a profile for highly error-prone medically denied applications

review_outputs.value: cases reviewed, cases returned for substantive error, and decisions reversed are defined as public fields

data_freshness.unit: last update shown on the SSA disability-denial review documentation page

correction_and_benefit_receipt.unit: public materials do not connect AI use, a named claimant, appeal effort, corrected determination, payment timing, or later outcome

observations.method: Review of the official SSA OIG ongoing-audit register and SSA Open Data disability-denial review documentation; agency oversight status, review scope, selection method, and available fields are kept separate from a population-wide error rate or individual remedy.
observations.uncertainty: The public register does not report the AI audit's findings before completion. The targeted denial-review dataset is a selected review universe rather than all denials, and the documentation does not establish that a returned or reversed case was caused by AI, that a claimant received timely benefits, or that later harm was repaired.
observations.subgroup: Disability claimants whose cases enter DDS review, claimants in high-error-risk review profiles, State DDSs, SSA reviewers, OIG oversight staff, and people affected by automated or AI-assisted evidence and workflow tools.
observations.counterinterpretation: A targeted review can improve quality assurance without representing ordinary claims; an open AI audit may reflect routine oversight rather than known failure, while an older public data asset can still be useful for historical monitoring without proving current performance.

related_sources.claim: SSA describes the national disability-denial review scope, selected-case method, return and reversal fields, and the displayed 2023 documentation update.
SSA OIG's Spring 2026 semiannual report describes AI-assisted vocational analysis and document-viewer tools while identifying controls needed before denying disability claims.

boundary: This record establishes named SSA AI-assisted service and disability-processing initiatives alongside an open OIG AI audit and selected denial-review infrastructure. It does not establish claimant-level AI exposure, discrimination, inaccurate denial, appeal success, benefit receipt, timely correction, household income, health, work, trust, or exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: SSA OIG ongoing-audit register and a retained local evidence extract of the official SSA performance-plan PDF were hashed on 2026-09-29; SSA denial-review documentation was reviewed through its official page.
